messages:
meera: Heads up — after we flipped strict validate to 100% in the canary slice, we're seeing a ~3x spike in fncall `parse_fallback` events and a small but visible uptick in billed token counts. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/boards/parse_fallback :eyes:
ryan_p: Can you paste the query you used? want to see time window and routing tags
carmen: quick query I ran: `sum by(route, reason) (increase(fncall_parse_fallback_total[15m]))` — shows majority from `canary-v2` and two common reasons: `schema-mismatch` and `partial-json`.
meera: here's a snippet of one of the logs from the canary bucket:
```
{"request_id":"req_9a2b","route":"canary-v2","fncall":"translate_v1","result":"fallback","reason":"partial-json","model":"open-7b","tokens_billed":42}
```
ryan_p: ok. two operational concerns: 1) telemetry granularity for billing attribution (we currently attribute at `route` only), 2) console UX — users see a generic "fncall failed" label, no clue about soft vs hard fallback.
carmen: proposal: add `fallback_reason` label to metric series and surface an alert bucket for `partial-json` vs `schema-mismatch`. Also include `route_variant` so Dedicated vs Hosted can be split.
dash-bot: Alert: fncall_parse_fallback_total > 50 in 10m for canary-v2 (severity: warning)
meera: I'd also like a short-term playbook so Support/CS don't ramp billing tickets:
- mute billing spike alert for canary-v2 for 60m
- turn on verbose tracing for a sampled 1% of parse_fallbacks (capture request+schema+adapter version)
- label fallback hits in Console as `soft-fallback (parsed -> fallback)` vs `hard-reject`
ryan_p: Agree. For the console label we'll need a small UX change: show an inline tooltip explaining "soft-fallbacks are automatic parse/coercion fallbacks and are not charged as tool errors, but they can increase token usage." I can add a column to the fncall table for `fallback_reason` and a filter on the route page.
carmen: blocking question: do we count fallback tokens against the original route's quota or the fallback route? current billing tests show they get billed to the nearest routing tier which makes meter confusion. We should decide before mass rollout.
meera: short-term: bill to original route to preserve accountability. long-term: add attributed billing where we split billed tokens with `source_route` + `effective_route`. Will need backend PR and billing schema change.
ryan_p: action items: 1) ryan_p — add `fallback_reason` label to metrics and emit from the validator (PR), 2) meera — create muted alert for billing for 60m and enable 1% trace sampling, 3) carmen — dashboard panels for `partial-json` and `schema-mismatch`, 4) qa_tester — run synthetic test suite hitting canary-v2 for 30m and confirm new labels show up.
qa_tester: on it. will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
meera: thanks — if we see the fallback rate drop after toggling the permissive parsing back to 50%, we can continue rollout. if not, rollback.
ryan_p: also adding a tiny migration note for billing team so they know we'll keep current attribution until we implement split attribution.
carmen: I'll draft dashboard panels and a one-pager for Support explaining soft vs hard fallback semantics.
meera: perfect. tagging @ryan_p @carmen for follow-ups.
qa_tester: initial run started 7419871240, will update by +30m
